newsitem.title: USA: Bell Atlantic/NYNEX opposed by NY Attorney General.
newsitem.headline: Bell Atlantic/NYNEX opposed by NY Attorney General.

text.p: New York Attorney General Dennis Vacco on Wednesday said the Bell Atlantic Corp NYNEX Corp merger could quash competition in the state, and is not in the public interest.
Vacco filed a brief to the New York Public Services Commission saying his department opposed the merger, after a year-long investigation.
"I am concerned that the proposed merger, as presently constituted, may adversely affect competition in New York telephone markets," Vacco said in a statement.

Vacco said that Bell Atlantic could have been an important competitor to NYNEX in the New York local phone market, and putting the two companies together could reinforce NYNEX's dominant position in residential and small business markets.
The Public Services Commission is expected to rule early in March on the merger.

The Justice Department and the Federal Communications Commission are the only other two approvals still outstanding in the merger, which is expected to be finalised by the end of the first quarter of 1997.
